framing: Three collisions on speed, agency, and the discipline of subtraction.
note: Themes: AI output vs outcome, agent-era agency, focus as positioning. Sources: SVPG, Stratechery, A Smart Bear.

sparks.title: SPEED WITHOUT SIGNAL
sparks.headline: Your velocity is not a metric

a.what: Teams are shipping visibly faster with AI while outcomes stay flat, because the old project model was built to produce output, not outcomes.

b.what: Pick proxy metrics: short-term signals you can move this week that actually predict long-term retention.

sparks.result: Ship rate is an output metric wearing an outcome's clothes. If no proxy metric moved this week, AI did not make you faster, it made you louder.
sparks.tick: Which proxy metric moved because you shipped faster this month?
sparks.provocation: Cagan's paradox is that AI adoption is climbing while results sit still, and the strong product companies are pulling further ahead rather than closing the gap. Biddle's answer predates AI: name the leading indicator you can move weekly, and let it judge your speed.

sparks.title: AGENCY IS SCARCE
sparks.headline: The bottleneck moved from hands to wants

a.what: Agents are a third paradigm, and because one person can direct many of them, AI no longer needs widescale human adoption for its impact to be profound.

b.what: Make something a small number of people want a lot, rather than something many people want a little.

sparks.result: Graham's rule now cuts both ways: the builders are also a small number of people who want something a lot. Wanting precisely is the new scarce resource.
sparks.result_underline: Wanting precisely is the new scarce resource
sparks.tick: What do you want specifically enough to hand an agent tonight?
sparks.provocation: Thompson's line is that AI still needs agency, it just does not need agency from that many people. That makes taste and initiative the constraint, not headcount or capital.

sparks.title: SUBTRACT TO POSITION
sparks.headline: Your calendar is your positioning statement

a.what: Only when you stop doing most things do you create the space to fully execute the few that decide whether you thrive or perish.

b.what: Positioning is a deliberate choice of competitive alternative, not a tagline you write at the end.

sparks.result: Positioning is not a document, it is a subtraction you can audit. Every yes you cannot defend is a competitor you just decided to be.
sparks.result_underline: a competitor you just decided to be
sparks.tick: What did you say yes to this week that blurs what you are?
sparks.provocation: Cohen catalogues what stopping creates space for: better customers, one real metric, a few modes of differentiation. Dunford names the thing that space is for, which is one clear alternative you beat.
